topic.subject: social
topic.title: Kingdoms, kings and early republics
topic.scope: janapadas and mahajanapadas, Magadha, Vajji gana, taxes, armies

misconceptions.statement: All janapadas were ruled by powerful kings who lived in grand palaces.
misconceptions.why: Students often conflate the term 'janapada' with the later, more centralized 'mahajanapada' empires.
misconceptions.fix: Janapadas were simply settlements where people set their feet; only some grew into powerful mahajanapadas with kings.

probe.question: Was every janapada ruled by a king with a large army?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because janapadas were always kingdoms.

misconceptions.statement: Mahajanapadas were modern countries with fixed borders and passports.
misconceptions.why: Students project their current understanding of nation-states onto ancient political structures.
misconceptions.fix: Mahajanapadas were territories controlled by rulers, but they lacked modern international borders or citizenship systems.

probe.question: Did people in a mahajanapada need a visa to travel to another?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, they had to show their papers at the border.

concepts.name: Forms of Governance: Monarchy vs. Gana-Sangha

misconceptions.statement: A Gana-Sangha was just another name for a kingdom.
misconceptions.why: Students assume all ancient political systems were monarchies because they are the most commonly discussed.
misconceptions.fix: A Gana-Sangha was a group-ruled system where many people shared power, unlike a monarchy where one king ruled.

probe.question: Who made the decisions in a Gana-Sangha?
probe.wrong_answer: The king made all the decisions alone.

misconceptions.statement: Ancient kings collected taxes in cash like we do today.
misconceptions.why: Students assume that economic systems have always been based on currency.
misconceptions.fix: Taxes were mostly collected in kind, such as crops, animal products, or labor, as money was not yet the primary medium.

probe.question: How did a farmer pay his tax to the king?
probe.wrong_answer: He went to the bank and paid in coins.
